svg.text: The version timeline: one number for the server
Concept 10 · SemVer MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH · what gets deployed changes = the version goes up · forward to go back
old users are forced to change too
a new feature, the old way still works
a small fix, the rest stays the same
the Pi deploys by itself, main
and the Pi without you SSHing in
a plain revert (the version back to 2.0.0) refused by the version guard in the job verify:
FAIL version 2.0.0 is LOWER than 2.0.1 on origin/main: the version may only go up.
a release tag = a page marker only the robot
sticks on: never make, move, or delete one
CHANGELOG.md: a notebook of changes for humans
- The checking and deploying robot (GitHub Actions …
- One version number for the server: backend 1.5.0 …
an ISO date YYYY-MM-DD is required (read by the version guard);
the tag v<version> holds its version's section (job tag-release)
One number in 10 places, guarded by scripts/check-version.mjs
what gets deployed changed without going up → the robot is red
raise it in backend and frontend: npm version 2.0.1 --no-git-tag-version
Visible from outside, without you SSHing in
the dashboard: v2.0.1 under the title (reload twice)
the Git tag v2.0.1 · the images …:2.0.1 and sha-<7>
the VPS and the Pi only deploy a version that has a tag
Own numbers that don't go up: firmware Node 1 1.7.x (Module 28) · Node 2 1.0.0 · DATA-CONTRACT.md 1.6 · PIN-MAP.md 7
Forward to go back: a revert brings back the code and the images, not the database content. A migration in one release only ADDS, so an old image still fits.
